key_facts: The patient is a man in his 40s
The patient has no significant medical history
The tumor is located on the left temporal scalp
The tumor is red, firm, and mobile
Dermoscopic evaluation shows irregular red lacunae without septa and irregular linear vessels
Histopathology shows a well-circumscribed dermal vascular tumor
The tumor extends to the superficial subcutaneous tissue
The tumor is composed of ectatic thin-walled vessels with multiple intravascular branching papillary structures
The structures are covered by swollen endothelial cells with numerous intracytoplasmic eosinophilic hyaline globules
PAS staining shows positive hyaline globules in the cytoplasm of endothelial cells
Tumor vessels are positive for CD-31 and negative for D2-40 and HHV-8

raw.rationale: The presence of ectatic thin-walled vessels with multiple intravascular branching papillary structures, covered by swollen endothelial cells with numerous intracytoplasmic eosinophilic hyaline globules, is characteristic of Papillary Hemangioma. Additionally, the positive PAS staining and CD-31 positivity, along with the negative D2-40 and HHV-8 staining, support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Hobnail Hemangioma
rejected.why: While Hobnail Hemangioma also presents with vascular structures, the specific features of papillary structures with hyaline globules are more indicative of Papillary Hemangioma.

rejected.label: Targetoid Hemosiderotic Hemangioma
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with a targetoid appearance and hemosiderin deposition, which are not mentioned in the case facts.

rejected.label: Pyogenic Granuloma
rejected.why: Pyogenic Granuloma usually appears as a rapidly growing, bleeding lesion, which does not match the slowly growing, firm nodule described in the vignette.
